  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most

    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point directly at the funnel that memory_31 and memory_86 claim to move, so those are the load-bearing memories and the ones worth spending the verification budget on. Both are stated in vague, effect-size-free language ('improved', 'durable lift') with no segment, duration, or counterfactual, which is exactly the shape of a claim that may have been compressed from a weaker original record; I want the archived experiment records to confirm magnitude, measurement window, and whether the lift persisted past week one. I deliberately do not spend budget on memory_73, which is already specific enough to act on: promotional_pricing is the tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing, but -12% retention makes it directly contrary to the sustainable-qualified-revenue objective, so competitor pressure should not be answered on price. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers and do not address the funnel decline; activation_messaging (memory_91) is the strong fallback if verification undercuts the onboarding memories, since it addresses the activation half of the problem. Downstream risk to flag: 'simplify onboarding' in practice means cutting required signup fields, and those fields are typically what qualifies and routes leads. That could quietly degrade the sales-assisted enterprise path that memory_44 says produces the best pipeline quality, converting a headline activation win into a qualified-revenue loss. So I scope the experiment to the self-serve SMB segment, leave the demo-request path untouched, and instrument downstream qualified-pipeline and 30-day retention rather than only completion rate. If the archive shows the original lifts were small, short-window, or measured only on completion rather than on revenue-relevant outcomes, I will shrink to a guarded test or switch to activation_messaging.
